sections.heading: What Is Definite Conjugation?
paragraphs: In Hungarian, we use definite conjugation when the object of the verb is specific or known.
Example: Látom a filmet. – I see the film.
Many verbs in this lesson already appear in definite form: olvasom, írom, nézem, hallom.

sections.heading: Accusative -t Ending
paragraphs: Hungarian marks objects with the -t ending.
If the noun ends in a vowel, you simply add -t.
If it ends in a consonant, it may take a linking vowel.

sections.heading: Simple Beginner Examples
paragraphs: Olvasom az újságot. – I’m reading the newspaper.
Írom az emailt. – I’m writing the email.
Nézem a filmet. – I’m watching the film.
Hallom a zajt. – I hear the noise.
